source: Canonical legacy identities 51-75 in data/v2-audit/current-question-audit.json order.

expansion_backlog_changes.motivational_tradeoff: breadth, energy, and new contact vs. trust, depth, and dependable connection
expansion_backlog_changes.insufficiency: Legacy items frequently substitute sociability or introversion; existing candidates establish the distinction but lack enough independent contexts for a large bank.

expansion_backlog_changes.motivational_tradeoff: protecting trust and continuity vs. restoring clarity and predictable structure
expansion_backlog_changes.insufficiency: Legacy material repeatedly assigns generic caution, reliability, or introversion to these colors without exposing why stability matters.

expansion_backlog_changes.motivational_tradeoff: restoring or owning the result vs. protecting coherence, evidence, and reliable execution
expansion_backlog_changes.insufficiency: Many legacy questions measure generic responsibility or competence; additional motive-centered parallel items are needed.

expansion_backlog_changes.motivational_tradeoff: which qualities or interaction patterns a person naturally seeks from others
expansion_backlog_changes.insufficiency: The first 75 legacy questions provide almost no valid PREFERENCE_IN_OTHERS evidence; the few examples are virtue-loaded or semantically unclear.

expansion_backlog_changes.motivational_tradeoff: what naturally attracts or rewards each color outside a problem state
expansion_backlog_changes.insufficiency: Reconstruction still contains disproportionate uncertainty, pressure, change, and problem scenarios relative to calm or enjoyable ordinary life.

expansion_backlog_changes.motivational_tradeoff: acting to produce a result vs. moving to discover an interesting possibility
expansion_backlog_changes.insufficiency: Legacy action language often conflates Red momentum with Blue spontaneity; more controlled non-work contrasts are needed.

current.prompt: I see uncertainty as an opportunity rather than a threat.

proposed.prompt: When an uncertain situation still offers a meaningful result, I prefer choosing a direction and pursuing progress rather than waiting for the uncertainty to disappear.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: progress under uncertainty vs. waiting for greater certainty
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether meaningful progress motivates action despite unresolved uncertainty.

questions.why: The legacy threat/opportunity framing can indicate optimism or Blue novelty; the revision anchors endorsement in Red progress and chosen direction.

current.prompt: I care about success, but not if it comes at the expense of others.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: personal success vs. avoiding harm to others
measurement.what_it_measures: Reluctance to pursue success when it harms other people.

questions.why: Avoiding success at others’ expense is an ethical position and universal virtue, not independently Yellow evidence.

current.prompt: I’m comfortable being rewarded more when I contribute more.

proposed.prompt: A reward tied directly to the result I achieve motivates me more than receiving the same recognition regardless of outcome.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: result-linked reward vs. equal recognition
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether outcome-linked recognition is more motivating than equal recognition.

questions.why: The legacy wording invites a fairness judgment about deserving more; the revision measures Red motivation from visible, outcome-linked reward.

current.prompt: In competition, I…

options.wording: play to win
play for the fun of it
play to keep things fair
play to improve my technique

proposed.prompt: During a friendly competition, what most naturally keeps you engaged?

options.label: A clear challenge and the chance to earn the result
The energy, surprises, and memorable moments along the way
The camaraderie and tradition that keep the group connected
The chance to understand patterns and refine my technique

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: winning challenge vs. experience energy vs. camaraderie vs. mastery
measurement.what_it_measures: Which source of reward sustains engagement in friendly competition.

questions.why: The legacy Yellow option makes fairness the color signal; the revision gives all four colors attractive, governed motivations.

current.prompt: I’m cautious about who I let into my inner circle.

proposed.prompt: I feel more settled deepening a dependable relationship than widening my circle with new connections.

replacement.prompt: I feel more settled deepening a dependable relationship than widening my circle with new connections.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: deepening dependable relationship vs. adding new connections
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether dependable relational depth feels more settling than widening one’s circle.

questions.why: Caution about an inner circle can reflect introversion or risk; the candidate directly measures Yellow relational depth against Blue breadth.

current.prompt: I feel responsible for supporting people I’ve committed to.

proposed.prompt: I feel responsible for supporting people I’ve committed to.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: supporting committed relationships vs. independently redirecting effort
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether an established commitment to people naturally creates a support obligation.

questions.why: Commitment is the explicit source of the support motivation, so the item measures governed Yellow loyalty rather than generic helpfulness.

current.prompt: If things feel dull or repetitive, I start looking for something more exciting to do.

proposed.prompt: Even when a routine works, I start looking for ways to make the experience feel fresh.

replacement.prompt: Even when a routine works, I start looking for ways to make the experience feel fresh.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: fresh experience vs. preserving a working routine
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether novelty remains attractive even when an existing routine works.

questions.why: The legacy wording can signal boredom tolerance or poor follow-through; the candidate preserves Blue freshness without implying abandonment.

current.prompt: I’m good at sticking with tasks until they’re fully completed.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: full completion vs. incomplete work
measurement.what_it_measures: Self-described ability to complete tasks.

questions.why: Being good at completing tasks is a competency and socially desirable self-claim, not independently Green evidence.

current.prompt: Money feels like a tool to create experiences, not an end goal.

proposed.prompt: When I have discretionary money, I’m more drawn to using it for a memorable experience than reserving it for a defined future purpose.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: experience now vs. reserved future purpose
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether a memorable experience is more attractive than a defined future use for discretionary money.

questions.why: The revision supplies a real choice and limits the scenario to discretionary money, reducing financial-security and moral confounds.

current.prompt: I feel calmer when I have a clear plan for what’s coming next.

proposed.prompt: When several next steps are possible, I prefer settling a clear plan for what comes next rather than preserving flexibility to decide later.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: clear plan now vs. flexibility to decide later
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether defined next steps feel preferable to preserving flexibility.

questions.why: The legacy item can measure anxiety; the revision compares two reasonable planning preferences.

current.prompt: I hesitate to make changes if they could negatively affect others.

proposed.prompt: A family tradition still matters, but its old format no longer fits everyone’s lives. What matters most as you help shape its next version?

options.label: Choose a workable version that keeps the tradition happening
Give it a new form that people will be excited to experience
Preserve the sense of connection and meaning people rely on
Understand the practical constraints and create a version with a predictable structure

replacement.prompt: A family tradition still matters, but its old format no longer fits everyone’s lives. What matters most as you help shape its next version?

options.wording: Choose a workable version that keeps the tradition happening
Give it a new form that people will be excited to experience
Preserve the sense of connection and meaning people rely on
Understand the practical constraints and create a version with a predictable structure

option_to_color.wording: Choose a workable version that keeps the tradition happening
Give it a new form that people will be excited to experience
Preserve the sense of connection and meaning people rely on
Understand the practical constraints and create a version with a predictable structure

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: purposeful result vs. renewed experience vs. continuity vs. coherent format
measurement.what_it_measures: Which priority guides change when a valued family tradition no longer fits.

questions.why: Hesitating because change could affect others is generic caution; the candidate reveals Yellow continuity alongside three equally legitimate motives.

current.prompt: I prefer knowing expectations ahead of time rather than figuring things out as I go.

proposed.prompt: In an unfamiliar situation, I prefer knowing the important expectations and constraints before I begin rather than discovering them as I go.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: known constraints before action vs. discovery through action
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether important constraints are sought before entering an unfamiliar situation.

questions.why: The revision makes Green clarity—not compliance or competence—the reason for preferring advance expectations.

current.prompt: I respect people who say what they mean, even if it comes across blunt.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: blunt candor vs. softened expression
measurement.what_it_measures: Respect for blunt, candid communication.

questions.why: Honesty is a universal virtue and bluntness/directness is explicitly insufficient as Red scoring evidence.

current.prompt: I tend to slow down decisions if I sense tension or discomfort between people.

proposed.prompt: When friends disagree about a shared plan and either option could work, I would rather keep discussing until the group feels comfortable than choose an option and let the tension fade afterward.

replacement.prompt: When friends disagree about a shared plan and either option could work, I would rather keep discussing until the group feels comfortable than choose an option and let the tension fade afterward.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: trust preservation vs. quick closure
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether protecting trust justifies leaving a decision open longer.

questions.why: The candidate makes the Yellow relational motive and real cost explicit instead of treating interpersonal discomfort itself as evidence.

current.prompt: I pay close attention to whether people follow through on what they say.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: demonstrated follow-through vs. stated intention
measurement.what_it_measures: Attention to whether other people keep their word.

questions.why: The item can reflect trust, conscientiousness, suspicion, or practical judgment and its Green assignment is not governed by the color model.

current.prompt: I try to stay organized so others can rely on me.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: organized reliability vs. less structured support
measurement.what_it_measures: Use of organization so other people can rely on the respondent.

questions.why: The statement combines organization and reliability as virtues; neither independently establishes Yellow.

current.prompt: When I’m focused, I…

options.wording: move fast and take action
talk through ideas out loud
support others and stay steady
go quiet and get precise

proposed.prompt: A time-sensitive problem appears and no one clearly owns it. What contribution comes most naturally to you first?

options.label: Set a workable first direction and coordinate the next action
Generate a few fast possibilities and rally people around the most promising one
Check the immediate effects on people and coordinate the support they will need
Verify the critical facts and define a reliable first response

replacement.prompt: A time-sensitive problem appears and no one clearly owns it. What contribution comes most naturally to you first?

options.wording: Set a workable first direction and coordinate the next action
Generate a few fast possibilities and rally people around the most promising one
Check the immediate effects on people and coordinate the support they will need
Verify the critical facts and define a reliable first response

option_to_color.wording: Set a workable first direction and coordinate the next action
Generate a few fast possibilities and rally people around the most promising one
Check the immediate effects on people and coordinate the support they will need
Verify the critical facts and define a reliable first response

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: ownership vs. possibilities vs. support vs. evidence
measurement.what_it_measures: What first attracts attention when an urgent problem has no clear owner.

questions.why: The legacy item mixes speed, talking, helping, and quiet precision as stereotypes; the candidate provides four useful motivations in one situation.

current.prompt: When I need a boundary, I…

options.wording: state it clearly
try to soften it with humor
worry about hurting feelings
explain it logically

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: clarity vs. humor vs. concern about feelings vs. logic
measurement.what_it_measures: Preferred way to express a personal boundary.

questions.why: Boundary style is learned and context-dependent; the Yellow option is pejoratively anxious while directness and logic are not standalone color signals.

current.prompt: People usually rely on me for…

options.wording: direction and urgency
energy and connection
support and stability
details and accuracy

proposed.prompt: A new colleague feels overwhelmed by several competing demands. What kind of help comes most naturally to you?

options.label: Identify the most important priority and help them take the next action
Help them see possibilities and regain some energy for the work
Help them identify which relationships and commitments need steady attention first
Organize the demands into clear steps, resources, and dependencies

replacement.prompt: A new colleague feels overwhelmed by several competing demands. What kind of help comes most naturally to you?

options.wording: Identify the most important priority and help them take the next action
Help them see possibilities and regain some energy for the work
Help them identify which relationships and commitments need steady attention first
Organize the demands into clear steps, resources, and dependencies

option_to_color.wording: Identify the most important priority and help them take the next action
Help them see possibilities and regain some energy for the work
Help them identify which relationships and commitments need steady attention first
Organize the demands into clear steps, resources, and dependencies

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: prioritization vs. possibilities vs. supportive steadiness vs. structure
measurement.what_it_measures: Which useful form of help comes naturally when someone faces competing demands.

questions.why: The legacy item asks respondents to claim strengths; the candidate observes a preferred helping contribution with balanced options.

current.prompt: I’m motivated when I feel connected to the people involved, not just the task.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: relational connection vs. task-only motivation
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether connection to involved people is a stronger motivator than the task alone.

questions.why: This is an exact duplicate of reviewed Question 41, which Batch 02 proposes to keep exactly.

current.prompt: I’m energized by new experiences, even if they’re unpredictable.

proposed.prompt: I’m energized by new experiences, even if they’re unpredictable.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: novel experience vs. predictability
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether new experience remains energizing despite unpredictability.

questions.why: The item cleanly measures Blue attraction to experience and novelty against a real uncertainty cost.

current.prompt: I stay focused when I know results depend on me.

proposed.prompt: I stay focused when I know results depend on me.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: result ownership vs. shared or process-based motivation
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether responsibility for the result naturally sharpens focus.

questions.why: The item ties motivation to responsibility for results, an established Red foundation, rather than generic responsibility alone.

current.prompt: When delegating, I…

options.wording: hand it off and expect ownership
ask who wants it and encourage them
make sure the person feels supported
define expectations and steps

proposed.prompt: You are delegating an important task to someone capable. What do you most naturally establish first?

options.label: The result they own and the authority they have to reach it
Room for them to shape the approach and bring their own energy
A dependable way to ask for support without losing ownership
The requirements, dependencies, and checkpoints that define success

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: owned result vs. autonomy vs. support channel vs. defined requirements
measurement.what_it_measures: Which foundation a person naturally establishes first when delegating meaningful ownership.

questions.why: The revision gives every color a competent delegation priority and removes the implication that only Yellow supports people.

current.prompt: My relationship with routines is…

options.wording: useful if it speeds results
hard to stick to unless it’s fun
I’ll do it if it helps others
I love routines—they reduce stress

proposed.prompt: An everyday routine is working well. What most makes it worth keeping?

options.label: It frees attention for the results and priorities that matter most
It leaves enough flexibility to keep the experience fresh
It makes shared life more dependable for the people involved
It produces predictable results and reduces avoidable uncertainty

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: freed attention vs. flexibility vs. shared continuity vs. predictability
measurement.what_it_measures: Which benefit makes a successful everyday routine worth preserving.

questions.why: The legacy options portray Blue as unable to persist and Green as stressed; the revision offers four constructive reasons to keep a routine.

current.prompt: Spontaneous plans sound more appealing to me than carefully planned ones.

proposed.prompt: Spontaneous plans sound more appealing to me than carefully planned ones.

measurement.motivational_tradeoff: spontaneity vs. advance planning
measurement.what_it_measures: Whether spontaneous plans feel more appealing than carefully planned ones.

questions.why: The item presents a clear Blue/Green preference with neither approach framed as more competent or mature.
